entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Asinius Gallus (35-33 BCE) was a Roman senator and son of Gaius Asinius Pollio and Quinctia. He held the office of Consul in 33 BCE and was the second husband of Vipsania, who was previously married to Tiberius. This union led to his imprisonment by Tiberius.









As a prominent figure in the late Roman Republic, Gallus played a significant role in the power struggles between the optimates and populares factions. His imprisonment by Tiberius in 33 BCE marked the beginning of the end of his political career.




Gallus' legacy is often overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, but his involvement in the tumultuous years leading up to the rise of the Roman Empire is a testament to his enduring importance in the annals of Roman history.
